title: Classification of dg-module diagrams by maps into projective models
statement:
Use the dg-category model structure of [lem-coef-dgcat-model-structure] and the module and Hom-complex conventions of [lem-coef-dg-module-projective-resolution]. Write $\mathsf{Hqe}$ for the ordinary localization of small dg categories at quasi-equivalences, and $\mathrm{Ch}(\mathbf Z)$ for cochain complexes of abelian groups. Let $\mathcal D$ be a small dg category over $\mathbf Z$. Let $\mathcal M$ be the category of covariant dg functors $\mathcal D\to\mathrm{Ch}(\mathbf Z)$, with its projective model structure: weak equivalences are objectwise quasi-isomorphisms, fibrations are objectwise degreewise surjections, and cofibrations are the maps having the left lifting property against trivial fibrations. This model structure exists, is enriched over complexes, is cofibrantly generated by maps with cofibrant domains and codomains, and all objects are fibrant. Let $\mathcal S$ be any full subcategory of $\mathcal M$ closed under objectwise quasi-isomorphisms in both directions. Write $\operatorname{Int}(\mathcal S)$ for the full dg category of cofibrant modules belonging to $\mathcal S$, with the actual complexes of module maps. For any small cofibrant dg category $\mathcal A$, let $D(\mathcal M^{\mathcal A})$ denote the localization of strict dg functors $\mathcal A\to\mathcal M$ at objectwise quasi-isomorphisms, and let $D(\mathcal M^{\mathcal A})_{\mathcal S}$ be its full subcategory on diagrams whose values belong to $\mathcal S$. There is a natural bijection
$$\operatorname{Hom}_{\mathsf{Hqe}}(\mathcal A,\operatorname{Int}(\mathcal S))\cong\operatorname{Iso}\bigl(D(\mathcal M^{\mathcal A})_{\mathcal S}\bigr),$$
where the right side is the set of isomorphism classes, and the left side is formed in universes large enough for $\operatorname{Int}(\mathcal S)$. The bijection sends a strict dg functor into $\operatorname{Int}(\mathcal S)$ to its underlying module diagram. In particular this is a classification of whole diagrams, not just of the collection of their values. The same bijection holds if $\operatorname{Int}(\mathcal S)$ is replaced by the full dg category of homotopically projective modules in $\mathcal S$.

source.place: Section 3, projective enriched diagram model structures preceding Proposition 3.2; Section 6, Lemma 6.2, specialized to dg modules; homotopically projective variant via projective-module replacement. Read online, absent from local literature. No Stacks tag supplies this dg-category theorem.

proof.text: Apply [lem-coef-enriched-projective-diagram-model] first to $\mathcal N=\mathrm{Ch}(\mathbf Z)$ and index $\mathcal D$. This constructs precisely the asserted projective model structure on $\mathcal M$, including enrichment, cofibrant generating domains and codomains, and fibrancy of all objects. Apply it again with target $\mathcal M$ and index $\mathcal A$ to obtain the projective model structure on strict $\mathcal A$-diagrams. By [lem-coef-dgcat-model-structure], the cofibrancy of $\mathcal A$ implies that its morphism complexes are cofibrant; hence evaluation of any cofibrant diagram is cofibrant in $\mathcal M$. These conclusions require no cofibrancy of the morphism complexes of $\mathcal D$.

source.place: Section 3, Definition 3.1, enriched-diagram model structures, and Proposition 3.3; compare Toën, https://arxiv.org/pdf/math/0408337, Section 3, Definition 3.1, enriched-diagram model structures, and Proposition 3.3. The external source is read online; the argument is written out here.

proof.text: Define $\mathcal A\otimes\mathcal D$ to have object pairs and morphism complexes $\mathcal A(a,a')\otimes_{\mathbf Z}\mathcal D(d,d')$, with tensor differential and composition using the graded symmetry. Currying identifies a strict $\mathcal A$-diagram of covariant $\mathcal D$-modules with a covariant module over $\mathcal A\otimes\mathcal D$, as follows. Put $H(a,d)=F(a)(d)$, and, for homogeneous $\alpha:a\to a'$ and $\delta:d\to d'$, put $H(\alpha\otimes\delta)=F(\alpha)_{d'}\circ F(a)(\delta)$. Graded naturality gives $F(a')(\delta)F(\alpha)_d=(-1)^{|\alpha||\delta|}F(\alpha)_{d'}F(a)(\delta)$, so compositions obey the tensor-category sign $(-1)^{|\delta'||\alpha|}$. Conversely restrict $H$ to $\alpha\otimes1$ and $1\otimes\delta$ to recover the two actions. A degree-$r$ transformation is a family of maps at $(a,d)$ satisfying the two graded commutation equations; these combine to the module equation with sign $(-1)^{r(|\alpha|+|\delta|)}$. The componentwise differential is $d\eta=d_G\eta-(-1)^r\eta d_F$ on both sides. Both categories have the same values at pairs of objects, the same complexes of graded module maps, and the same objectwise quasi-isomorphisms and surjections. Thus their projective model structures agree, by the lifting definition of cofibrations. A projectively cofibrant module $P$ is homotopically projective: for any objectwise acyclic $N$, apply the enriched model axiom of [lem-coef-enriched-projective-diagram-model] to $0\to P$ and the trivial fibration $N\to0$. It says that $\underline{\operatorname{Hom}}(P,N)\to0$ is a quasi-isomorphism. Apply [lem-coef-dg-module-projective-resolution] to $(\mathcal A\otimes\mathcal D)^{\mathrm{op}}$ (a homogeneous left action $bm$ is read as the right action $mb=(-1)^{|b||m|}bm$ over the opposite; this turns the signed left-module map equation into the right-module equation in that node). Between these cofibrant modules, morphisms in the localized diagram category are therefore $H^0$ of the actual module-map complexes. In particular an isomorphism between two cofibrant diagrams has representatives in both directions whose composites differ from identities by boundaries; it is represented by a chain homotopy equivalence of module diagrams, hence by an objectwise quasi-isomorphism.

The external source is read online; the argument is written out here.

proof.text: By [lem-coef-dgcat-model-structure], every morphism $\mathcal A\to\operatorname{Int}(\mathcal S)$ in $\mathsf{Hqe}$ has a strict dg representative and equality is model-category homotopy. Choose a cofibrant cylinder $\mathcal A\amalg\mathcal A\hookrightarrow\mathcal C\xrightarrow{p}\mathcal A$ with inclusions $i_0,i_1$ and $pi_t=1$. Its middle object is cofibrant since the first map and the initial maps of both copies of $\mathcal A$ are cofibrations. Thus all morphism complexes of $\mathcal C$ and $\mathcal A$ are cofibrant. Each $i_t$ and $p$ is a quasi-equivalence, by two-out-of-three. Apply [lem-coef-locally-cofibrant-dg-restriction] with target $\mathcal M$: on localized diagram categories $p^*$ is an equivalence and $i_0^*,i_1^*$ are both its inverses since $i_t^*p^*=1$. Consequently they are naturally isomorphic. A cylinder homotopy $H:\mathcal C\to\operatorname{Int}(\mathcal S)$ therefore has isomorphic endpoint module diagrams. Their values are in $\mathcal S$, and this is an isomorphism in the full subcategory $D(\mathcal M^{\mathcal A})_{\mathcal S}$. This proves that the proposed map on $\mathsf{Hqe}$ is well defined. The same argument works with homotopically projective values, since this step does not need cofibrancy of the values of $H$.

source.place: Section 6, Lemma 6.2, well-definedness via Proposition 3.2; compare Toën, https://arxiv.org/pdf/math/0408337, Section 6, Lemma 6.2, well-definedness via Proposition 3.2. The external source is read online; the argument is written out here.

proof.text: Given any diagram $F$ with values in $\mathcal S$, factor $0\to F$ in the projective diagram model structure as $0\to QF\xrightarrow{q}F$, with $QF$ cofibrant and $q$ a trivial fibration. By step 1 and [lem-coef-enriched-projective-diagram-model], every $QF(a)$ is cofibrant. Since $q(a)$ is a quasi-isomorphism and $F(a)\in\mathcal S$, saturation in both directions gives $QF(a)\in\mathcal S$. Thus $QF$ is a strict dg functor into $\operatorname{Int}(\mathcal S)$, and $q$ identifies its image with $F$ in the localized diagram category. This proves surjectivity for whole diagrams, including their action maps.

source.place: Section 4, Sub-lemma 4.4; Section 6, Lemma 6.2, surjectivity; compare Toën, https://arxiv.org/pdf/math/0408337, Section 4, Sub-lemma 4.4; Section 6, Lemma 6.2, surjectivity. The external source is read online; the argument is written out here.

proof.text: Suppose strict dg functors $F,G:\mathcal A\to\operatorname{Int}(\mathcal S)$ give isomorphic localized diagrams. Their cofibrant replacements $QF,QG$ are isomorphic there. By step 2 and [lem-coef-dg-module-projective-resolution], a closed module map $QF\to QG$ represents this isomorphism and is an objectwise quasi-isomorphism. Therefore $F,G$ are connected by the zigzag $F\leftarrow QF\to QG\to G$ of objectwise quasi-isomorphisms between diagrams with cofibrant values in $\mathcal S$. For any arrow $\alpha:U\to V$ of such a zigzag, use [lem-coef-enriched-projective-diagram-model] to factor $(\alpha,1):U\amalg V\to V$ as a diagram cofibration $j:U\amalg V\to Z$ followed by a trivial fibration $p:Z\to V$. Evaluation preserves cofibrations by step 1. Each coproduct inclusion is a cofibration at every value, since the other summand is cofibrant (it is a pushout of its initial cofibration). Hence both maps $U\to Z$ and $V\to Z$ are objectwise cofibrations. Their composites with $p$ are $\alpha$ and $1$, so both maps are objectwise quasi-isomorphisms by two-out-of-three. Their values and the values of $Z$ are cofibrant. Moreover $Z(a)\in\mathcal S$ since $p(a)$ is a quasi-isomorphism to $V(a)$. We have replaced each arrow by a span of objectwise trivial cofibrations, entirely within cofibrant values in $\mathcal S$. No closure of $\mathcal S$ under coproducts is used: $U\amalg V$ is only an intermediate object in the ambient model category.

source.place: Section 4, Sub-lemma 4.5, reduction to trivial cofibrations (explicit coproduct factorization); compare Toën, https://arxiv.org/pdf/math/0408337, Section 4, Sub-lemma 4.5, reduction to trivial cofibrations (explicit coproduct factorization). The external source is read online; the argument is written out here.

proof.text:
Form a dg category $\mathcal E_{\mathcal S}$ whose objects are trivial cofibrations $c:P\to Q$ in $\mathcal M$ with $P,Q$ cofibrant and in $\mathcal S$. Between $c:P\to Q$ and $c':P'\to Q'$ take the strict-square complex
$$\underline{\operatorname{Hom}}(P,P')\times_{\underline{\operatorname{Hom}}(P,Q')}\underline{\operatorname{Hom}}(Q,Q'),$$
with differential and composition componentwise. It is a dg category because the square equation is preserved by both operations. Let $e_0,e_1$ be its source and target dg functors to $\operatorname{Int}(\mathcal S)$, and let $s$ send $P$ to $1_P$. For the trivial cofibration $c$ and the fibrant object $Q'$, the enriched model axiom in [lem-coef-enriched-projective-diagram-model] makes $\underline{\operatorname{Hom}}(Q,Q')\to\underline{\operatorname{Hom}}(P,Q')$ a degreewise surjective quasi-isomorphism. Its pullback is exactly the map of Hom complexes induced by $e_0$. This pullback is again a surjective quasi-isomorphism: its kernel is the same acyclic kernel $K$. To check acyclicity of the kernel of a surjective quasi-isomorphism $t$, a kernel cycle $z$ is a boundary $dx$ in the source by injectivity on cohomology. The element $t(x)$ is a cycle; surjectivity on cohomology gives a source cycle $y$ with $t(x)-t(y)=dv$. Lift $v$ to $w$ using degreewise surjectivity; then $x-y-dw$ is a kernel primitive of $z$. For any degree-$n$ cycle in the target, choose a degree-$n$ lift; its differential is a cycle in $K^{n+1}$, hence a boundary, so subtracting an element of $K^n$ gives a cycle lift. If a cycle maps to a boundary, lift a primitive and subtract its differential; the remaining cycle is in $K$ and is a boundary there. This proves surjectivity and injectivity on cohomology in every degree. Thus $e_0$ is quasi-fully faithful; it is essentially surjective since $e_0s=1$. By [lem-coef-dgcat-model-structure] it is a quasi-equivalence and becomes invertible in $\mathsf{Hqe}$. Since $e_0s=e_1s=1$, the section $s$ is its inverse and $e_0=e_1$ in $\mathsf{Hqe}$. Every objectwise trivial-cofibration transformation $U\to V$ from step 5 defines a strict dg functor $\mathcal A\to\mathcal E_{\mathcal S}$: naturality is exactly the strict-square equation in each degree. Composing with $e_0,e_1$ shows $[U]=[V]$ in $\mathsf{Hqe}$. Applying this to the spans of step 5 proves $[F]=[G]$, hence injectivity. This constructs the needed comparison for diagrams and never infers it merely from objectwise isomorphisms.

source.place: Section 4, Sub-lemma 4.5, arrow-category argument, expanded at the level of Hom complexes; compare Toën, https://arxiv.org/pdf/math/0408337, Section 4, Sub-lemma 4.5, arrow-category argument, expanded at the level of Hom complexes. The external source is read online; the argument is written out here.

proof.text: Let $\mathcal P_{\mathcal S}$ be the full dg category of homotopically projective modules in $\mathcal S$. The enriched-model argument in step 2, applied to $\mathcal D$-modules, proves that every cofibrant module is homotopically projective. The inclusion $j:\operatorname{Int}(\mathcal S)\hookrightarrow\mathcal P_{\mathcal S}$ is fully faithful on actual Hom complexes. For any $P\in\mathcal P_{\mathcal S}$ choose a projective-model cofibrant replacement $QP\to P$ using [lem-coef-enriched-projective-diagram-model]. It lies in $\mathcal S$ by saturation, and both endpoints are homotopically projective. By [lem-coef-dg-module-projective-resolution] this quasi-isomorphism is a chain homotopy equivalence, hence an isomorphism in $H^0\mathcal P_{\mathcal S}$. Therefore $j$ is a quasi-equivalence and becomes invertible in $\mathsf{Hqe}$ by [lem-coef-dgcat-model-structure]. Composing with its inverse gives the asserted bijection for $\mathcal P_{\mathcal S}$. To verify its description on a strict functor $T:\mathcal A\to\mathcal P_{\mathcal S}$, represent $j^{-1}[T]$ by a strict $F:\mathcal A\to\operatorname{Int}(\mathcal S)$, which is possible since $\mathcal A$ is cofibrant. Then $jF$ and $T$ are homotopic, and step 3 (with homotopically projective values) makes their underlying module diagrams isomorphic. Thus this variant also sends each strict functor to its entire underlying diagram.

source.place: Section 6, Lemma 6.2, homotopically projective variant via replacement; compare Toën, https://arxiv.org/pdf/math/0408337, Section 6, Lemma 6.2, homotopically projective variant via replacement. The external source is read online; the argument is written out here.

proof.text: For a strict dg functor $u:\mathcal A'\to\mathcal A$ between cofibrant test categories, both operations on the classification send a representative $F$ to the underlying diagram $F\circ u$. Hence the bijections commute with restriction in the test category; the well-definedness in step 3 makes this independent of representatives. The same statement holds after the inclusion $j$ of step 7. Every morphism between these cofibrant test categories in $\mathsf{Hqe}$ has a strict representative by [lem-coef-dgcat-model-structure]. If two representatives are cylinder-homotopic, composing their cylinder homotopy with $F$ and applying step 3 makes the pulled-back diagrams isomorphic. Consequently restriction on isomorphism classes depends only on the $\mathsf{Hqe}$ morphism, and the displayed compatibility proves naturality on the full subcategory of cofibrant test categories in $\mathsf{Hqe}$. All auxiliary dg categories, including $\mathcal E_{\mathcal S}$ and $\mathcal P_{\mathcal S}$, are taken in an enlarged universe as permitted by [lem-coef-dgcat-model-structure]; no smallness assumption on $\mathcal S$ in the original universe was used.
